comments.author: limaoscarjuliet
comments.story: TSA Doesn’t Care That Its Luggage Locks Have Been Hacked
comments.why: Bags can be opened with a pen bypassing locks.
comments.text: Most bags can be opened and closed with a ball point pen WITHOUT A TRACE completely bypassing any locks. [VIDEO]

comments.author: chiph
comments.why: Demonstrates opening zippers with a pen without trace.
comments.text: So use a ballpoint pen on the zipper. You jam it in the nylon teeth so they separate, and you can loot the bag. Afterwards, use the zipper pull to heal the teeth and there's no trace you were in there. [VIDEO] To counter this (and unauthorized use of a TSA key), wrap your bag in industrial cling-wrap plastic. You should also go right to baggage claim when you land. Most airports don't have someone looking at the bag claim receipts, so thieves can walk right out with a bag.

comments.author: lotu
comments.story: Lockpickers 3-D Print TSA Master Luggage Keys from Leaked Photos
comments.text: Honestly I doubt it will become a big deal outside of the tech community. Most people realize luggage locks aren't really there to protect against a determined adversary, or a person with a ballpoint pen [VIDEO]

comments.author: edko
comments.story: Lockpickers 3-D Print TSA Master Luggage Keys from Leaked Photos
comments.why: Zippers can be opened with a pen and reclosed.
comments.text: The chain always breaks by the weakest link. Considering that you can very easily open the zipper with a ballpoint pen ( [VIDEO] ), and close it again as if it was never open, that the secret of the lock was revealed is irrelevant.
